mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over one month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over two months signals weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST declines > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.2pp and payroll employment (PAYEMS) shows no growth over one month, it signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS growth is <= 0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) at an annualized rate of more than 2% over two quarters signals strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) does not adjust by more than 0.1%, it signals a potential inflationary pressure mismatch, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS adjusts <= 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2pp over one month signals the end of the cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp during late-cycle expansion.
